name: Pytheas of Massalia
summary: A Greek astronomer from Marseille sails the Atlantic coasts, circles Britain and reports Thule and the amber coast; route reconstructed from fragments in Strabo, Pliny and Diodorus.

stops.note: Sets out; only the fragments quoted by later writers survive, so all dates are approximate.
Cunliffe's reconstruction has him cross Gaul by the Aude-Garonne isthmus route.
Reaches the Atlantic at the Gironde estuary.
Names the island off the Osismii coast of Armorica.
Describes tin-mining Britons who smelt ore and trade it at a tidal island.
The tidal tin island reached by wagon at low water.
Names the northern cape of Britain and measures long midsummer days.
Reports a land six days' sail north of Britain, near the frozen sea, where the sun barely sets.
Names the south-eastern corner of Britain, completing the island's triangle.
Reports an island where amber washes ashore and is sold to the Teutones.
Returns and writes On the Ocean.

sources.cite: Barry Cunliffe, The Extraordinary Voyage of Pytheas the Greek, London 2001
C. H. Roseman, Pytheas of Massalia: On the Ocean, Chicago 1994
